extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in mathematical logic / computability theory
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formal criteria for computable (total and partial) functions, their indexing (Kleene normal form), reducibility, undecidability results (halting problem, Gödel incompleteness), the S-m-n (parameter) theorem, Rice's theorem, and a register-machine model equivalent to recursive partial functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of computable partial function
rubrics_metrics.description: An m-place partial function f is computable iff there is an effective procedure such that (a) given an m-tuple a in dom f, the procedure produces f(a); and (b) given an m-tuple a not in dom f, the procedure produces no output at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends the definition previously given for total functions; computability means there is an effective method that halts with the value exactly when the function is defined and never halts otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computability characterized by effective enumerability (Theorem 36C)
rubrics_metrics.description: An m-place partial function f is computable iff f (as an (m+1)-ary relation) is effectively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: from an enumeration of the relation output the corresponding (m+1)-tuple when it appears; conversely, simulate staggered computations for each input tuple to enumerate existing outputs. This links procedural computability and enumerability of the graph/relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of recursive partial function
rubrics_metrics.description: A recursive partial function is a partial function that, as a relation, is recursively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: 'recursive partial function' is an indivisible phrase — such a function need not be recursive as a relation (i.e., decidable). For total functions the terminology coincides with earlier usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence for total functions (Theorem 36D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f : N^m → N be total. Then f is a recursive partial function iff f is recursive (as a relation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f is recursive as a relation and total, then both f and its complement are recursively enumerable, so f is decidable; conversely total recursive functions are recursively enumerable relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and the universal function (definition of [[e]]_m)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each e ∈ N define the m-place partial function [[e]]_m by [[e]]_m(a1,...,am) = U(μk e, a1,...,am, k ∈ T_m), where the right-hand side is undefined if no such k exists. Equivalently, a ∈ dom([[e]]_m) iff ∃k [e, a1,...,am, k ∈ T_m], and when defined the value is U(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an indexing of all m-place recursive partial functions: e is thought of as the 'program' or index, and U, T_m are the fixed universal and test predicates arising from representability/arithmetization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleene Normal Form Theorem (1943)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The (m+1)-place partial function (e,a1,...,am) ↦ [[e]]_m(a1,...,am) is recursive. (b) For each e ≥ 0, [[e]]_m is an m-place recursive partial function. (c) Any m-place recursive partial function equals [[e]]_m for some e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: there is a universal computable partial function and every recursive partial function has an index. The theorem is used to reason about universality, diagonalization, and undecidability arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undecidability of totality of indices (Theorem 36E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set {e | [[e]]_1 is total} is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction via diagonalization: assume decidability to build a total function that cannot coincide with any indexed total function, leading to contradiction. Shows there is no effective test to tell from an index whether the corresponding partial function is total.

rubrics_metrics.name: The halting/definedness set K (Theorem 36F)
rubrics_metrics.description: K = {a | [[a]]_1(a) is defined} is recursively enumerable but not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K is r.e. because membership is witnessed by the existence of a k with (a,a,k) ∈ T1; nonrecursiveness follows by diagonal arguments producing a total function that contradicts any recursiveness assumption. K is the classic 'diagonal' set central to halting/uncomputability proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolvability of the halting problem (Corollary 36G)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation {(e,a) | [[e]]_1(a) is defined} is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, there is no effective procedure that given program e and input a decides whether the computation halts with a value. This follows from nonrecursiveness of K by simple reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of r.e. relations as domains (Theorem 36H)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation on N is recursively enumerable iff it is the domain of some recursive partial function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: given r.e. Q use a recursive relation R with Q(a) ⇔ ∃b (a,b) ∈ R and define f(a)=μb[(a,b)∈R]. Conversely, domains of recursive partial functions are r.e. This yields the canonical enumeration We = dom([[e]]_1) of all r.e. sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Many-one reducibility preserves recursion and enumerability (Lemma 36I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ≤_m B via total recursive f, then (a) if B is recursive then A is recursive; (b) if B is recursively enumerable then A is recursively enumerable; (c) if B is at arithmetical level Σ_n (or Π_n) then so is A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use composition with the reducing function to transfer predicates/quantifiers; this is the standard tool for showing undecidability and for placing sets in the arithmetical hierarchy by reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computability perspective on Gödel incompleteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Th(N) is not recursively axiomatizable: Th(N) is not r.e., hence any recursively axiomatizable (r.e.) subtheory of Th(N) must be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction: encode the r.e. set K into sentences so that membership in K corresponds to truth in Th(N); then any r.e. axiomatizable theory T ⊆ Th(N) omits some true sentence, giving incompleteness. This supplies an alternative proof of incompleteness via computability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter theorem (S-m-n theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each m ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1 there is a recursive function ρ such that for any e, a (parameters), b (arguments), [[e]]_{m+n}(a1,...,am,b1,...,bn) = [[ρ(e,a1,...,am)]]_n(b1,...,bn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning: one can effectively produce from an index e and fixed parameters a an index for the partially applied program. Used to construct reductions and to prove many undecidability results (e.g., show {a | W_a = ∅} is not recursive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application pattern: using parameter theorem for reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove nonrecursiveness of a property A of indices, often produce a total recursive g such that a ∈ K ⇔ g(a) ∈ A (or a ∉ K ⇔ g(a) ∈ A) using ρ to manufacture programs whose behavior depends on [[a]]_1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: show {a | W_a = ∅} is not recursive by producing g(a) with [[g(a)]]_1(b) = [[a]]_1(a) so dom[[g(a)]]_1 is empty iff [[a]]_1(a) undefined. This is the standard reduction technique in computability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice's theorem (Theorem 36J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C be a set of one-place recursive partial functions. Then the set {e | [[e]]_1 ∈ C} of indices of members of C is recursive iff either C is empty or C contains all one-place recursive partial functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nontrivial extensional semantic properties of computable functions (properties depending only on the function, not on program) are undecidable. Proof uses parameter theorem and diagonalization to reduce K to the index set IC unless C is trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register machine model and instruction semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A register machine has finitely many registers each storing a natural number and a finite program whose instructions are: I_r (increment r), D_r (decrement r; if nonzero decrement and skip next instruction, if zero just continue), T_q (transfer q: jump q instructions forward/backwards; halts if target instruction out of range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of small programs (clear register, move number, addition) illustrate how to encode basic arithmetic. The D_r instruction's conditional skip behavior is crucial for control flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a register-machine program 'calculates' a partial function
rubrics_metrics.description: Program P calculates an n-place partial function f iff: (i) starting with a1,...,an in registers 1..n, if f(a1,...,an) is defined then the machine eventually halts seeking the (p+1)st instruction and leaves f(a1,...,an) in register n+1 (and halts by stepping past program end); (ii) if f(a1,...,an) is undefined then the computation never terminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the operational notion of 'computes' for register machines: halting-with-output corresponds to definedness, divergence to undefinedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of models: register machines capture recursive partial functions (Theorem 36K)
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial function f has a register-machine program that calculates it iff f is a recursive partial function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline: arithmetize computations to show machine-computable functions are recursive; conversely show the primitive building blocks and closure operations used to generate recursive functions are implementable by register machines. Thus register machines characterize the class of recursive partial functions.
